response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.player_id) AS cnt FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON ma.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id), t AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM c) SELECT c.player_id, c.cnt AS award_count, CASE WHEN t.total IS NULL OR t.total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE CAST(c.cnt AS REAL) / t.total END AS fraction FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE t.total IS NOT NULL ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST, c.player_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each manager_award row counts as one record; players are matched via player_id, and manager_award rows whose player_id is not in player are ignored (the total is the sum of counts over players in the player table).
If the total is 0 the fraction is NULL (avoiding division by zero) and such rows still appear, sorted last; a NULL total (empty player table) returns no rows.
Ties in fraction are broken by player_id ascending for determinism.
